messages.content: Let’s settle the hotels now. Use the selected San Jose flights and the $338 compact car. I want the full four-night cost for each lodging plan, including tax and parking, and I want to know whether changing hotels Saturday is actually worthwhile.

I checked the three current rate details. The Monterey waterfront hotel is $312 per night for four nights, with 14% room tax and $35 nightly self-parking. Its rate can be canceled without charge through 6:00 p.m. two days before arrival; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. That makes the room $1,248, tax $174.72, and parking $140, for a lodging total of $1,562.72.
Is the parking fee itself taxed or are there any resort fees hiding behind that total?

The booking terms show no resort or destination fee, and the displayed $35 parking charge is the final nightly parking amount rather than a pre-tax figure. So $1,562.72 is the complete hotel-and-parking total on the information currently shown. A room incidental hold would not be part of the final cost unless you charge something to it.
Okay. Do Carmel next.

The Carmel inn is $344 nightly, or $1,376 for four nights. Its room tax is 12%, adding $165.12, and self-parking is included. There is no separate resort fee listed. The complete lodging total is $1,541.12. Cancellation is free until 3:00 p.m. three days before arrival; a later cancellation costs the first night plus tax.
So Carmel is actually about twenty-two dollars less than the waterfront hotel, despite the higher room rate.
Correct. Carmel is $21.60 less over four nights because parking is included and its tax rate is lower.
Now calculate the split carefully. Two nights at $279 in Monterey, then two at $329 in Carmel. What are the parking and cancellation rules on those exact rates?

For the split plan, the $279 Monterey rate has 14% room tax, $35 nightly parking, and no resort fee. Two nights come to $558, plus $78.12 tax and $70 parking, or $706.12. That reservation is cancellable through 6:00 p.m. two days before its Thursday check-in. The $329 Carmel rate has 12% tax and included parking: $658 plus $78.96 tax, or $736.96. It can be canceled through 3:00 p.m. three days before its Saturday check-in. Together, the split stay totals $1,443.08.
That is a more meaningful difference. Put all three beside the fixed flight and car costs so I can see the trip totals.

Using $972 for the two flights and $338 for the compact car, the fixed subtotal is $1,310. Adding lodging gives: Monterey waterfront, $2,872.72; Carmel for all four nights, $2,851.12; split stay, $2,753.08. These totals cover flights, the quoted rental-car total, room tax, and hotel parking. They do not add fuel, checked-bag charges, meals, or activity admission.
How does each location work for what we planned? Thursday evening in Monterey, aquarium Friday, Big Sur Saturday, Carmel and Point Lobos Sunday, then the 1:20 flight Monday.

The waterfront hotel is strongest for Thursday evening and Friday: you can stay parked and reach Cannery Row and the aquarium easily. It is also straightforward for Monday’s drive to SJC. The tradeoff is driving back north after Big Sur and again after Carmel or Point Lobos. The all-Carmel stay is best for Saturday and Sunday and puts you closer to the Big Sur approach, but Thursday’s arrival and Friday’s aquarium visit require extra driving and parking in Monterey. Monday remains practical from Carmel, though you should allow roughly 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours for SJC before adding airport-return time and your desired check-in margin.
And the split? I’m concerned that checking out Saturday means our Big Sur day starts with packing and luggage in the car.

That is the main drawback. You would check out of Monterey Saturday morning, load everything into the rental car, and either carry it through the Big Sur outing or ask the Carmel inn to hold it before check-in. A pre-activity luggage drop would avoid leaving bags in the car, but it adds a detour and depends on the inn confirming early storage. The move itself likely consumes 45 to 75 minutes once packing, checkout, driving, unloading, and check-in or storage are included.
Would moving Friday evening be smarter, after the aquarium?

Operationally, yes: it would keep Saturday clear and avoid taking luggage toward Big Sur. But it would also shorten Friday evening in Monterey, and the quoted two-and-two rates are tied to Thursday-Friday in Monterey and Saturday-Sunday in Carmel. Changing to one Monterey night and three Carmel nights needs fresh pricing and could erase some of the savings.
Stay with the quoted plan. Quantify what we save by accepting the Saturday move.

The split saves $98.04 compared with four nights in Carmel and $119.64 compared with four nights at the Monterey waterfront hotel. For two people, that is about $49 to $60 each. In return, you gain the best base for each half of the itinerary, but you spend part of Saturday moving and need confirmed luggage storage to avoid keeping bags in the car.
That doesn’t sound like enough savings by itself. Is there enough location value to make up for it?

Only marginally. The split improves Friday access to the aquarium and Sunday access to Carmel and Point Lobos, but an all-Carmel stay already works well for three of the four main sightseeing days and costs just $98.04 more. It also eliminates the Saturday checkout, two separate cancellation deadlines, and the luggage issue. The waterfront-only plan is harder to justify because it costs the most while adding return drives from the southern activities.
Then choose Carmel for all four nights. Give me the exact booking-stage summary and flag anything that still needs confirmation.

Choose the Carmel inn for all four nights: four nights at $344 are $1,376, 12% room tax is $165.12, and included self-parking keeps the lodging total at $1,541.12. With the selected SJC flights at $972 for two and the compact rental estimate of $338, the current flight-car-hotel total is $2,851.12. The hotel rate is refundable until 3:00 p.m. three days before arrival; after that, the stated penalty is one night plus tax. Before payment, confirm that the live checkout still shows no added property fee, included parking for one vehicle, and the same cancellation deadline. The flight fare and bag charges also remain subject to the airline checkout, and the $338 rental is still an estimate rather than a reserved counter total. Nothing has been booked.
